title: Context fingerprint TTL pinning workflow for per-model long-sequence performance
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: implement a reproducible onboarding workflow that generates a compact 'context fingerprint' for each model+route and uses that fingerprint to recommend and enforce per-model KV cache TTL pinning. This ticket covers the pipeline to build fingerprints from sampled sequence distributions, map fingerprints to TTL suggestions and pinning policies, validate those policies in staging, and publish the resulting performance profile to the catalog for use by routing and the runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A CRON pipeline (or triggered job) consumes sampled sequence metadata and computes a stable context fingerprint for new model revisions.
Fingerprint->TTL mapping rules are codified and versioned (yaml) and can be applied automatically during onboarding.
A staging rollout validates that TTL pinning reduces cold-KV tail latency for long sequences without regressing median latency on short sequences.
Published profiles appear in the model catalog with a timestamp, fingerprint hash, recommended TTL, and an associated validation run ID.
Console shows per-model fingerprint, TTL, and validation metrics; alerts fire if live traffic diverges from sampled distribution by configured thresholds.
Integration tests exercise fallback behavior when a fingerprint is unknown (graceful defaults + telemetry).
comments: 2026-02-15 - Triage: Identified need after multiple long-context incidents where cold KV cache spikes occurred for models with heavy tail sequences. Proposal to move from per-model heuristics to fingerprint-based TTL pinning.

2026-02-20 - PoC: Ran a PoC that hashed sequence-length histogram + token-type macro features into a 128-bit fingerprint. TTL suggestions (2m/10m/1h) reduced 95th percentile token latency by ~18% on longseq workloads in canary pool.

2026-02-25 - Design review: PM (Aisha) requested explicit validation and rollback criteria. Design suggested storing validation run metadata (traffic sample, canary window, control vs pinned cohorts).

2026-03-02 - Engineering sync: Decided to implement fingerprint generation in the onboarding pipeline (not runtime) to keep runtime lightweight. Runtime will read published profiles and expose a fast fingerprint equality check for routing.

2026-03-05 - Trade-off discussion: Tight TTL pinning reduces warmups but may increase memory usage on high-cardinality fingerprints. Agreed mitigation: limit pinned TTLs per model to top-k fingerprints by traffic share and fall back to shared LRU cache for rare fingerprints.
2026-03-08 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4892 adds fingerprint ingestion endpoint and model-catalog integration (WIP). Assigned to Marcelo for follow-up.

2026-03-10 - Integration test: Running end-to-end validation in staging against a synthetic mix (70% short, 30% long). Observed 12% token-cost increase for one model due to overly aggressive TTL; created follow-up task ENG-78190 to add a cost-aware pin selector.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint encoder and deterministic hashing (edge cases for empty/degenerate histograms).
Property tests to ensure minor variations in sampling order do not change fingerprint (stability).
Staging rollout: create pinned cohort vs control cohort at 1% traffic for 48h, compare 50/95/99 token latency and token cost.
Chaos test: simulate KV eviction storms and ensure fallback cache keeps requests serviceable with graceful degradation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fingerprint cardinality explosion for models with polymorphic prompts. Mitigation: cap stored fingerprints per model and fall back to a shared LRU eviction group for low-traffic fingerprints.
Risk: Incorrect TTL increases memory and token cost. Mitigation: cost-aware selection, validate on staging, and require manual override for P0 customers.
Risk: Stale fingerprints after model revision. Mitigation: fingerprint contains model revision hash and onboarding pipeline re-calculates on every revision or flagged retrain.
Risk: Privacy-sensitive features leaking via fingerprint. Mitigation: fingerprint built only from aggregated histograms (no raw tokens) and reviewed by security team.
